name: Collagen peptides
lead: Collagen peptides, also called hydrolysed collagen, are short amino acid chains made by breaking down animal collagen from bovine, marine or porcine sources. They are sold as powders and drinks for skin elasticity, hair, nails and joints.

Early meta-analyses reported improvements in skin hydration and elasticity, but later analyses suggest the effect shrinks or disappears in higher-quality trials and those not funded by industry, so claims of visible anti-ageing benefit remain contested.

paras: Digested collagen peptides, particularly hydroxyproline-containing di- and tripeptides, are absorbed and may signal fibroblasts to make more collagen and hyaluronic acid. Alternatively, they simply supply amino acids that the body uses like any other protein. Human evidence for a specific signalling role is not conclusive.

Side effects are generally mild, such as bloating or an unpleasant taste, and allergy is possible with marine or bovine sources. Supplements are lightly regulated, and heavy metal contamination has been flagged in some products. There is no evidence of meaningful hair-growth effect.
